Subject: Post-call: Hyperscaler feature comparison, test runbook and actions

Hi Julia / John —

Thanks again for the discussion this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can move from discovery to a short, measurable run of parity tests against what you saw from the hyperscaler POC.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary asks: function/tool calling parity, structured JSON outputs for downstream parsers, and streaming behavior (partial JSON / mid-stream aborts).
- Non-functional: latency targets (tail p95 < 250ms for short-turn prompts), cost sensitivity for high-throughput embed/generate workloads, and security requirements (audit logs + KMS).
- Hyperscaler behavior you noticed: deterministic tool-call markers that stream partial JSON chunks and a specific response-splitting behavior when a schema is long.

Attached: redwood-hyperscaler-diff-runbook.pdf (draft runbook) and sample-prompt-set.csv — both are runnable test artifacts.

Proposed short runbook (we want to validate in a 2–4 hour sandbox window):
1) Function-call echo (sanity): tool-call request -> tool invoked -> response captured. Success = exact argument payload intact and invocation metadata in trace.
2) JSON schema enforcement: long-structure gen with schema; success = parsable JSON with schema validation + clear failure payload when invalid.
3) Structured streaming: large JSON output streamed in chunks; success = each chunk is syntactically valid appendable JSON (or clearly signaled continuation tokens), and ability to resume/abort.
4) Abort/early-cancel: client-initiated cancel mid-stream -> backend drops tokens within 50ms of cancel + logs cancel event.
5) Throughput / cost baseline: run 1k light prompts and 200 heavy structured prompts to capture invoice-able token counts and per-second throughput.

Asks for Streamline team:
- Confirm which of the above test cases are high priority (1–3 prioritized ideally).
- Provide a 2-hour sandbox window (we suggested Tue 2027-06-08 09:00–11:00 PDT).
- Share any IP/secret access method for your tool endpoints if you want us to call back into your infra for the function-call tests (otherwise we will simulate tool behavior).

Next internal owners: Rishi will lead the runbook execution and perf capture; Aditya will coordinate billing/procurement details if you need an incognito test billing arrangement.

Open items to discuss in the next sync: how we report per-token cost vs hyperscaler at different batch sizes, and whether you want streaming over SSE vs chunked HTTP.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar invites once you confirm the window.

Thanks Neha — this is great and clear. A couple of clarifying Qs before we lock the window: 

1) Streaming semantics: when you say "structured streaming" can Redwood deliver partial JSON objects that are syntactically appendable, or do you rely on boundary tokens that client code must stitch? Our current consumer expects to parse every chunk as valid JSON fragment (they re-assemble arrays on the fly). We need to know whether Redwood will guarantee either of those patterns or provide a compatibility layer.

2) Abort behavior: important to our SLOs. If we cancel a long-running generation, do you guarantee that the model stops generating within a bounded time and that the billing reflects partial token emission? The hyperscaler we tested reported a delayed stop and counted tokens for ~500ms after cancel.

3) Cost reporting: can you capture per-request token counts and map them to expected per-token cost in the runbook CSV so our finance team can compare apples-to-apples?

We can confirm Tue 2027-06-08 09:00–11:00 PDT if Rishi is good with the instrumentation. Also looping procurement (procurement@streamline.ai) to discuss any short-term test billing needs.

-Julia

Thanks — quick technical notes and a slightly expanded test checklist. I’ll own run execution on Tue if the window holds.

Streaming semantics:
- Redwood supports two streaming modes: chunked HTTP streaming (chunk per token/group) and SSE with event markers. For structured output we provide a "structured-stream" mode where the runtime emits framing markers and per-chunk schema hints (e.g., "cont" / "end" tokens) so clients can append safely. That means the chunks are not always individually valid full JSON objects, but we provide an SDK helper (open-source snippet) that reassembles and validates progressively. If you need strict per-chunk-valid JSON, we can run the test both ways and show the tradeoffs (latency vs parser complexity).

Abort semantics and billing:
- Abort request is honored at the runtime level; observable stop time is typically within 20–150ms depending on GPU batch flushing. Billing is token-emission-based and we log both produced tokens and pre-allocated batch tokens; our runbook CSV will include both counts so you can replicate the hyperscaler view.

Function/tool calling:
- We implement the function-calling spec (argument JSON + metadata) and emit an explicit invocation event in traces. When invoking external endpoints, we support both direct callback (we POST to your endpoint) or a simulated local hook to avoid sharing creds. We will include invocation headers in traces and a trace id in the response for correlation.

Expanded test checklist (Runbook v1):
A) Tool-call echo (owner: Rishi) — confirm invocation payload fidelity, invocation trace id, retry semantics.
B) Strict-chunk JSON streaming (owner: Rishi) — run with SDK reassembler and with per-chunk-valid JSON mode (two runs).
C) Abort & billing correlation (owner: Rishi / Neha) — issue mid-gen cancel at t=0.5s and t=1.5s for heavy prompts; capture stop latency and token counts.
D) Schema-failure handling (owner: Rishi) — deliberately send prompts that violate schema and check failure payload + error code consistency.
E) Perf baseline vs hyperscaler (owner: Aditya) — measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and token billing for 1k light / 200 heavy runs.
F) Security trace review (owner: Neha / Procurement) — capture audit log snippet for a sample run and show KMS envelope ids.

Success criteria (short):
- Tool-call fidelity: 100% argument parity across 50 runs.
- Structured streaming: reassembler produces valid JSON with <1% reassembly errors in 200 heavy-stream runs.
- Abort: stop latency < 250ms and billing recorded equals emitted tokens.
- Perf: p95 within 20% of hyperscaler for similar-sized models or a documented delta with cost delta.

I attached runbook-v1.md with explicit curl commands and SDK snippets for test harness. If Streamline wants us to call back into their staging endpoint, deliver a short-lived credential or we can simulate the endpoint with a local echo.

-Rishi
